title: Gradient at a point on a curve
competency: Find the gradient of the tangent line to a curve at a point.

keywords.def: A line that touches a curve at one point and has its steepness there.
The point where the tangent line touches the curve.

en.text: Move the second point Q towards P: the secant lines turn into the tangent line. So the gradient at a is what (f(x) − f(a))/(x − a) approaches as x approaches a. Factor (difference of squares or cubes) or rationalise, cancel x − a, then put x = a. For y = x² the gradient is 2a.

am.text: ሁለተኛውን ነጥብ Q ወደ P ስናቀርብ ሴካንቶቹ ታንጀንት ይሆናሉ። በ a ላይ ያለው ግራዲየንት x ወደ a ሲቀርብ (f(x) − f(a))/(x − a) የሚቀርበው ነው። ለ y = x² ግራዲየንቱ 2a ነው።

screens.title: Secants that turn
screens.ask: Q moves along a curve closer and closer to P. The secant line PQ becomes
screens.after:
Each secant PQ has slope (f(a + h) − f(a))/h.
As Q moves to P, h gets closer to 0.
The secant turns into the tangent at P. Its slope is the gradient there.

screens.title: From secant to tangent
paras: P is (a, f(a)) and Q is (a + h, f(a + h)).
As h gets closer to 0, Q moves to P and PQ becomes the tangent.
screens.note: Slope of the tangent = instantaneous rate of change.

screens.title: Q slides to P on y = x²
screens.ask: P = (1, 1) on y = x². Tap each Q. Watch the slope of PQ.
items: The slopes approach 2. The tangent at P has gradient 2.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A line that touches a curve at one point and has its steepness there.
The point where the tangent line touches the curve.

screens.text: Find the gradient of the tangent to y = x² at (a, a²):
screens.why:
Secant slope: (x² − a²)/(x − a).
Factor: x² − a² = (x − a)(x + a).
Cancel x − a: x + a.
Let x approach a: a + a = 2a.
Trap: a² is the y-value, not the gradient.

screens.title: Gradients on y = x²
screens.ask: The dots lie on y = x². The line is the tangent at (2, 4). Tap the dots.

points.info: Gradient 2(0) = 0: the tangent is the x-axis.

points.name: P
points.info: Gradient 2(2) = 4. Tangent: y = 4x − 4. It touches the curve only here.

screens.ask: Find the gradient of f(x) = 3x² − 5x + 4 at x = 2: ___
screens.why:
f(2) = 12 − 10 + 4 = 6.
f(x) − 6 = 3x² − 5x − 2 = (x − 2)(3x + 1).
Divide by x − 2: 3x + 1.
Let x approach 2: 3(2) + 1 = 7.
(In general the gradient at a is 6a − 5.)

screens.ask: Find the gradient of g(x) = √x at x = 4: ___
Find the gradient of f(x) = 1/x at (2, 1/2): ___
screens.why:
1/x − 1/2 = (2 − x)/(2x).
Divide by x − 2: (2 − x)/(2x(x − 2)) = −1/(2x).
Let x approach 2: −1/(2 × 2) = −1/4.
Negative: 1/x falls as x grows.

screens.text: Find the gradient of f(x) = x³ at (a, a³):
screens.why:
Start with (x³ − a³)/(x − a).
Difference of cubes: x³ − a³ = (x − a)(x² + ax + a²).
Cancel x − a: x² + ax + a².
Let x approach a: a² + a² + a² = 3a².

screens.ask: Work backwards on y = x²: at which x is the tangent gradient −6? x = ___
screens.why:
On y = x² the gradient at x = a is 2a.
Set 2a = −6.
So a = −3.
Check: 2(−3) = −6. ✓

items.text: Find the gradients of f(x) = x² at x = −1 and at x = 4:
items.why:
The gradient of x² at x = a is 2a.
At x = −1: 2(−1) = −2.
At x = 4: 2(4) = 8.
1 and 16 are the y-values, not the gradients.

items.ask: Find the gradient of f(x) = 3x² − 5x + 4 at x = 2: ___
items.why:
The gradient of 3x² − 5x + 4 at a is 6a − 5.
At a = 2: 6(2) − 5 = 12 − 5 = 7.

items.text: Find the gradient of f(x) = 3x² − 5x + 4 at x = −√2:
items.why:
The gradient at a is 6a − 5.
Put a = −√2: 6(−√2) − 5.
= −6√2 − 5.
Trap: 6√2 − 5 drops the minus sign of a.

items.ask: Find the gradient of g(x) = √x at x = 4: ___
Find the gradient of f(x) = 1/x at (2, 1/2): ___

items.text: Find the gradient of f(x) = x³ at (a, a³):
items.why:
(x³ − a³)/(x − a) = x² + ax + a².
Let x approach a: 3a².
Trap: 3a forgets that each of the three terms becomes a².

test.ask: Find the gradient of f(x) = x² at x = 7: ___
test.why:
The gradient of x² at a is 2a.
2 × 7 = 14.
Trap: 49 is f(7), the y-value.

test.ask: Find the gradient of f(x) = x² + 5x at x = 1: ___
test.why:
f(1) = 6. f(x) − 6 = x² + 5x − 6 = (x − 1)(x + 6).
Cancel x − 1: x + 6.
Let x approach 1: 1 + 6 = 7.
(Same as 2a + 5 at a = 1.)

test.ask: Find the gradient of f(x) = x³ at x = 2: ___
test.why:
The gradient of x³ at a is 3a².
3 × 2² = 3 × 4 = 12.

test.text: What does the gradient of a curve at a point equal?
opts: the slope of the tangent there
test.ans: the slope of the tangent there
test.why:
The gradient at P is the slope of the tangent at P.
It is the limit of secant slopes as Q moves to P.
One secant gives only an average rate. The y-value is not a slope.

test.ask: Find the gradient of f(x) = 2/x at x = 1: ___
test.why:
f(1) = 2. 2/x − 2 = 2(1 − x)/x.
Divide by x − 1: −2/x.
Let x approach 1: −2/1 = −2.
